source_workbook.context: Welcome to the Delaware SHIP Community Data Resource Guide! The State Health Improvement Plan (SHIP) team, comprised of University of Delaware and Delaware Division of Public Health, and KIDS COUNT in Delaware developed this resource to support community-based organizations (CBOs) in identifying relevant state data sets that can help enhance health and wellness within their communities. This resource provides background information, outlines key data categories and measures, and includes publication dates, data source timelines, links to the most current data, and access to archived reports. We welcome suggestions for additional resources. For questions, feedback, or recommendations, please contact Info@DelawareSHIP.org or visit our website at DelawareSHIP.org (Last Updated July 2026)

sources.name: America's Health Rankings (United Health Foundation)
sources.background:
America’s Health Rankings provides an analysis of national health on a state-by-state basis by evaluating a historical and comprehensive set of health, environmental and socioeconomic data to determine national health benchmarks and state rankings.
The platform analyzes over 250 measures from more than 50 publicly available data sources to assess the nation’s health and well-being on a wide range of demographics including race and ethnicity, gender, education, age, disability status and income, among others. Data is based on public-use data sets, such as the U.S. Census and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), the world’s largest, annual population-based telephone survey of over 400,000 people.
notes:
- shows Delaware's ranking in comparison to US and other states
- including data by race and ethnicity, age, gender, income, education and metropolitan status, among other demographics
- state measure rankings include social and economic factors, physical environment, clinical care, behaviors, health outcomes, overall, and demographics
